history.recommendation_text: The Board recommended that the Administration conduct a cost-benefit analysis before engaging personnel through UNOPS, UNDP or third- party service providers and clearly define the identity of personnel to ensure the correct application of the legal framework and contractual responsibilities.
history.administration_response: Through the entry into force of two new financial agreements as of 1 January 2024, the UNOPS contracted workforce is clearly identified under the legal and contractual framework of UNOPS. Department of Political and Peacebuilding Affairs: In line with the Board’s recommendation in paragraph 309, the Department commissioned a cost-benefit analysis of its current financial agreements with UNOPS for the Standby Team project. The study, conducted by an external expert, was finalized in December 2022, and shared with the Board in March 2023 during field work for A/78/5 (Vol. I). The recommendations of the study informed the review and update of the 2023 financial agreements. The report finds that the current arrangement between the Department and UNOPS is cost-effective, efficient, and fit for purpose and in compliance with the applicable United Nations administrative rules and regulations. The Department reiterates that it also presented a cost- benefit analysis to the Board in May 2023, illustrating the efficiency and cost- effectiveness of UNOPS support for the Department’s innovation projects. Based on the recommendations set out in the cost-benefit analysis, negotiations for a new financial agreement under UNOPS management commencing in the second quarter of 2024 are in progress, which will ensure full adherence to legal and contractual obligations, particularly regarding the clear definition of personnel identities and selection processes. The cost benefit analysis is ongoing as the Department of Operational Support is negotiating a United Nations-wide agreement with UNOPS. The Development Coordination Office proposes that it be removed from this recommendation as the Office will no longer be the owner of the agreement.
history.board_assessment: Given that the Office of Information and Communications Technology has not yet provided the implementation status, the Board considers this recommendation to be under implementation.

history.recommendation_text: The Board recommended that the Administration conduct a cost-benefit analysis before engaging personnel through UNOPS, UNDP or third-party service providers and clearly define the identity of personnel to ensure the correct application of the legal framework and contractual responsibilities.
history.administration_response: The Department of Political and Peacebuilding Affairs (Mediation Support Unit) commissioned a cost-benefit analysis of its current financial agreements with UNOPS for the project of the Standby Team of Senior Mediation Advisers. The study, conducted by an external expert, was finalized in December 2022 and shared with the Board in March 2023 during field work relating to A/78/5 (Vol. I). In the report, the current arrangement between the Department of Political and Peacebuilding Affairs and the United Nations Office for Project Services (UNOPS) was found to be cost-effective, efficient, fit for purpose and compliant with the applicable administrative rules and regulations of the United Nations. In line with the new memorandum of understanding between UNOPS and the Secretariat released in May 2024, in December 2024 the Department of Political and Peacebuilding Affairs finalized two new financial agreements with UNOPS to cover the operation of the mechanism of the Standby Team of Senior Mediation Advisers in 2025. The Department also presented a cost-benefit analysis to the Board in May 2023, which illustrates the efficiency and cost- effectiveness of UNOPS support to the Department’s innovation projects. In October 2024, the Department finalized a new financial agreement modality with UNOPS for innovation initiatives, following the updated memorandum of understanding between UNOPS and the Secretariat released in May. Office of Information and Communications Technology: In his report on the refined elements of the information and communications technology strategy (A/79/339), the Secretary-General outlined the information and communications technology (ICT) operating model and reiterated that the use of the contractual services of private technology and professional services companies would be guided by procurement processes, leverage the mutual recognition of contracts and capitalize on new or existing contracts to acquire skill sets to allow improved service delivery with the ability to scale up or down, depending on the demand and requirements. The Secretary-General also indicates that the ratio of 55 per cent of contractors to 45 per cent of staff in an ICT workforce is, in general, accepted in line with industry standard practice in the ICT area.
history.board_assessment: Given that a cost-benefit analysis has been conducted, the Board considers this recommendation to be implemented.
